# uscha

> Uscha is a spec-driven, tool-agnostic methodology for software development with LLM coding agents. Its doctrine: measured beats narrated — gates that read facts block; gates that guess over prose advise. The agent executes, the method governs, evidence decides, the human approves.

Uscha closes the central hole of the "open loop" paradigm, where the agent decides
for itself when it is finished. Instead, work moves through a fixed pipeline of
phases (idea → discovery → spec → adr/constitution → build → qa loop → verify →
production) whose gates are answered by deterministic, auditable artifacts — a
ledger (QA-LEDGER.json), coverage, golden suites — never by the agent's own
narration. The QA loop is bounded: it converges or escalates to a human, and the
human always approves the merge.

Five rules form the spine: (1) no code without SPEC + ACCEPTANCE; (2) the truth
lives in versioned files, not in the chat; (3) the human always approves the
merge; (4) tests must assert — the gate is never weakened; (5) migrations are
anchored with a mechanically captured golden suite the agent must never author.

The ceremony floor is not flat. Fast-path (kit 1.57+, ADR-003) lets a provably
small change skip the up-front ceremony — the engine measures the real diff
(files, lines, protected paths) and decides; the agent's word is never taken for
it, and rigor is a one-way ratchet (a human may force more, never less). Spec-drift
(ADR-005) flags specs gone stale relative to their code from git dates — advisory,
it never gates. Neither skips human approval or asserting tests.

For existing systems, Reverse Discovery (kit 1.64+, ADR-009) extracts facts (a
system map and a mechanically captured golden), then authors CANDIDATE claims about
behavior in quarantine (discovery/*.md, each with typed evidence and confidence).
Nothing is promoted without a recorded human verdict — preserve, fix or undefined —
in BEHAVIOR-LEDGER.md; the curation-check gate measures this and a candidate with no
verdict blocks the PR, naming itself (INV-CURATION-01). A fix declares its expected
divergence, which the golden oracle then checks; an advisory roundtrip report traces
promoted candidates back into code by id. That id-level roundtrip is deliberately not
semantic matching; the measured semantic round trip is bench-roundtrip (below).

The underlying thesis ("the diamond"): specs are the source code, the LLM is the
compiler, reverse discovery is the decompiler — and code becomes a regenerable build
artifact, so the spec package + behavior ledger is the canonical asset of a system.
Truth-pass status: the human-judgment layer (curation, oracle, id-level roundtrip) is
real and shipped; implementation replaceability is now demonstrated for bounded systems
(the Diamond Bench, kit 1.74–1.99, four blind compilers across two vendors — Haiku, Sonnet, Opus and OpenAI Codex gpt-5.5: 8 of 12 archetypes (11 Python + 1 JavaScript, one
multi-unit) regenerate to the same system, mechanically certified by a withheld oracle
— ADR-017/018/020/025/028/029); semantic round-trip is now REAL but bounded (kit 1.85/1.90, ADR-030 amended: bench-roundtrip measures how
much of the human-authored IR the mechanical reverse organs can anchor in each compiled artifact
-- 0.815, static AND behaviour footing since the 12 bench oracles were curated with per-case
AC tags (kit 1.90, ADR-030 amended; it read 0.062 with behaviour UNMEASURED before that, a named
absence rather than a zero); it anchors names and behaviour, and regenerates no spec); full code regenerability of arbitrary systems
remains VISION, deferred until it can be measured. The shared drift/discovery engine is NOT deferred: ADR-011 REJECTED it as
architecture -- spec-drift compares commit dates and reverse discovery proposes content, so there is no extraction engine to share.
The framing is positioning where it says VISION, a measured mechanism where it says REAL, and a decision on the record where it
says REJECTED.

The kit (v1.99.0, MIT license) ships 9 skills for 7 coding agents — Claude Code,
Codex, Cursor, VS Code / GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Cline and pi (Earendil); only Claude Code and Codex are exercised against a real agent, the other five are verified by placement + read-back only —
plus a pure-Python engine (qa_ledger.py, 53 subcommands, zero runtime dependencies)
that ingests evidence from 11 language stacks. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
(Python 3.8+). Install for one agent, or `--target all`:
`npx --yes @andresmassello/uscha@latest install --target claude`

## Docs

- [Home](https://uscha.dev): landing page — the method, the five rules, the nine skills, the engine's numbers
- [Why uscha exists](https://uscha.dev/why): essay — open loop vs. measured graph, who answers the gates, why the loop is caged
- [How it works](https://uscha.dev/how): three diagrams — greenfield discovery, brownfield reverse discovery, and the curation mechanism (one human verdict, everything else measured)
- [The diamond](https://uscha.dev/diamond): the thesis — specs as source code, code as build artifact, with the REAL vs VISION vs REJECTED truth-pass table
- [2-day developer course](https://uscha.dev/docs/uscha-dev-course-EN.html): from zero to production — day 1 greenfield (discovery), day 2 migration (characterize, reverse-discovery)
- [Complete documentation](https://uscha.dev/docs/uscha-claude-code-doc-EN.html): the whole method in one place — rules, phases, every skill, gates and the ledger
- [Field note 001 — treasury migration](https://uscha.dev/field-notes/001-treasury-migration): a real, anonymized migration — the five times the measured graph contradicted an apparent "done"; not in production, readiness 79.4, stated up front
- [The paper](https://uscha.dev/docs/paper/uscha-paper.html): formal treatment — a fact-gated, tool-agnostic methodology for specification-driven development with LLM coding agents ([PDF](https://uscha.dev/docs/paper/uscha-paper.pdf))
